    html_preview: false

---

`r if (isTRUE(params$reduced)) "**Reduced render: this is not the report.** It runs every step on less data and gives no timing verdict." else ""`

This report gives the 1×/2×/4× scaling evidence `STYLE.md` asks for, for
`duckhts_bam_mate_overlap_counts()`. The function reads coordinate-sorted
alignments once, on one worker. It holds the first mate of a pair whose mate
starts inside it until the mate arrives, and it counts the positions that both
mates align to in fixed counters. So its work grows with the alignments it
reads, and its memory grows with the mates it holds at once. No earlier report
measures this function; this is its first baseline.

## Workloads

- **Real.** chr1 of the 1000 Genomes 30× CRAM of HG00403, staged as a CRAM
  slice (registry artifact `bam_mismatch_hg00403_chr1_cram`, staged by
  `benchmarks/bam_mismatch_stage.R`), read with the registered GRCh38 FASTA
  (`liftover_grch38_fasta`) as its reference. The render checks the slice
  against its registered identity and the FASTA against its registered size
  and MD5 before it measures. Those checks read both files in full, so every
  measured run reads from a warm page cache. Three regions double the
  alignments: chr1 up to the 25% and the 50% quantiles of the alignment start
  positions, and the whole contig. The mates held at once are what the data
  give. The render derives them, and they are not fixed.
- **Synthetic.** Generated at render time, untimed: DuckDB writes SAM text, and
  the samtools that the RBCFTools package bundles sorts it and indexes it as
  BAM. A contig holds fragment families 1,000 bases apart. A family is P pairs
  of 150-base reads whose read 1s all start at one position. Read 2 of pair j
  starts d = 1 + (97 j mod 149) bases after its read 1. So it shares 150 − d
  positions (1 to 149) with its read 1, and every read 1 is held until its
  read 2 arrives. All P read 1s of a family are held at once: the held-mate
  count of a contig is P, and the contig has 2 × families × P alignments. One
  pair in 16 has one substituted read-2 base, a known disagreement. One pair
  in 16 has a read 2 with MAPQ 10, which the default `min_mapq` of 20 leaves
  out; its read 1 is held and then dropped when the scan passes its mate's
  start. Seven contigs give three series that share the 1× contig
  (families × P):
  - alignments at a fixed held-mate count: 4 × 100,000, 8 × 100,000 and
    16 × 100,000;
  - held mates at fixed alignments: 4 × 100,000, 2 × 200,000 and
    1 × 400,000;
  - both: 4 × 100,000, 4 × 200,000 and 4 × 400,000.

  A family stands for a deep amplicon, or a deep pileup of short fragments:
  the stress shape for held mates. The amplicon sequence and the base
  qualities are fixed, so this BAM compresses far better than real data.

## Held mates, derived from the input

The function holds a kept alignment when its mate starts inside it and no
mate of the same name is held. It releases the held mate when its mate
arrives, or when the scan passes the mate's start without it. A record with
the name of a held mate that does not pair with it is left out, and the held
mate stays held. The render derives the number of mates held at once from
each input, with SQL over `read_bam()` and without the function:

- an alignment is kept by the function's default filters: MAPQ at least 20, no
  flag of 3844, paired, mate mapped, and mate on the same contig;
- the first kept alignment of a name, by position, is held when its mate
  starts inside it (`PNEXT` from `POS` up to its reference end);
- the held alignment is released at its mate's position when the name has
  two kept alignments that pair: one is read 1 and the other read 2, and each
  names the other's start. Otherwise it is dropped before the first alignment
  past the position it names.

A drop comes before every hold at its position. A hold and a release by an
arriving mate at one position come in file order, which `read_bam()` does not
give for CRAM. So the derived count is bounded. The lower bound is the most
mates held after all the alignments of a position. The upper bound adds back
the mates that arriving mates release at that position, as if every hold
there came first. The render also runs the function untimed with
`max_pending` at the upper bound, which must succeed, and at one below the
lower bound, which must fail with its limit error. The budget uses the upper
bound. The derivation assumes that no name has more than two kept alignments
and that every kept alignment has a CIGAR that matches its sequence; the
render checks both.

## Budget, declared before measuring

The overhead is the median peak RSS of three empty runs that start the CLI,
load the extension and scan nothing.

The ceiling of each input is overhead + 3 × its live state. It is a gate on
the peak RSS: the render stops if any observation exceeds its ceiling or
spills. The live state is:

- the counters: 95 × 95 × 16 cells of 8 bytes, 1,155,200 bytes;
- the held mates, from the held-mate count H of the input (its upper bound)
  and D, the bytes of CIGAR, sequence and qualities of its longest kept
  alignment:
  - the entries, 320 bytes each and allocated 1,024 at a time, each with
    16 bytes in the heap and the free list: 1,024 × ⌈H / 1,024⌉ × 336 bytes;
  - the name table, 2 × C + 1 slots of 24 bytes, where C is the smallest
    1,024 × 2<sup>k</sup> that is at least H. While the table doubles, the
    half-size table it replaces is live too, so 24 × (3 C + 2) bytes, or
    24 × 2,049 bytes when C is 1,024;
  - the CIGAR, sequence and qualities of each held mate, H × (D + 24) bytes;
    the 24 bytes cover the allocator's header and rounding. An entry is
    reused and keeps its largest buffer, so D is the longest kept alignment;
- htslib's state for the file. For the CRAM, 32 MiB is allowed for the
  container in hand (its compressed and uncompressed blocks and its decoded
  records); this part is an allowance, not derived from the input. The
  reference of the slice in hand and of the slice before it is added to it.
  Without decoder threads, htslib asks for the reference of one slice's span
  (`third_party/htslib/cram/cram_decode.c` lines 2452–2456).
  `cram_get_ref()` loads only that span, unless the span is at least half the
  contig (`third_party/htslib/cram/cram_io.c` lines 3248–3256). It frees the
  previous span after it loads the next one (lines 3340–3347). The render
  takes the widest pair of consecutive slices in each region from the CRAM
  index. For the BAM, 4 MiB is allowed for its blocks, the record and the
  index.

The render also stops if a time exponent of the real series is above 1.25 at
either doubling, or if its 1× run on one thread takes less than 5 s, the least
that `STYLE.md` accepts for a timing verdict. The synthetic series read their
1× contig in well under 5 s. So they get the memory verdict in full, and their
times are reported without a verdict, as `STYLE.md` provides.

## Protocol

Every observation is one fresh DuckDB CLI process under `/usr/bin/time`. The
JSON profiler gives the query latency and DuckDB's peak buffer and temporary
bytes, and `/usr/bin/time` gives the peak RSS. The host is shared, so the
render is pinned to eight cores (8 to 15) and runs at scheduling priority −15
(`nice`), which every measured process inherits. The host load at the start
is recorded, and the spread of the repetitions shows what interference
remained. `max_temp_directory_size` is zero, so a spill fails the render;
DuckDB's memory limit is left at its default, which the report records. Each
cell has three repetitions at one thread and at four threads, in an order
that alternates sizes. The function has one worker, so the thread setting
should not change it, and the four-thread cells show whether that holds. Each
query reduces the rows of the function to their number, the shared positions
and the disagreements, so every row is produced and consumed. The R wrapper
only builds this SQL call; it is not timed here.

The render also checks the counts. On each synthetic contig, every row of the
output must equal the counts that follow from the design, which R computes
from the amplicon, the qualities and the pair rules alone. On the real data,
every row of the output in the 400 kb around the position with the most held
mates must equal the same count made in SQL from `read_bam()` and
`cigar_aligned_blocks()`, as the SQL tests make it. That SQL count keeps only
alignments that can share a position with their mate: each mate must start
before the other ends.

``` sh
nice -n -15 taskset -c 8-15 Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("benchmarks/benchmark_bam_mate_overlap_counts.Rmd")'
```

The render needs RBCFTools 1.24-1.1.0 or later for its samtools. The
parameter `reduced` (`params = list(reduced = TRUE)`, with an `output_dir`
outside the repository) runs every step on less data: a 2 Mb window of the
CRAM around the most held mates (chr1:124,000,001–126,000,000) and synthetic
families of a hundredth of the pairs. It keeps every gate except the timing
verdict, writes its runs to a temporary file and says at its top that it is
not the report. It checks the code end to end in a few minutes.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
```

```{r benchmark, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
stopifnot(requireNamespace("duckhtsbench", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE))
# A reduced render checks every step on less data; see the render command.
reduced <- isTRUE(params$reduced)
Sys.setenv(DUCKHTSBENCH_REGISTRY = normalizePath(
  "r/duckhtsbench/inst/benchmark_registry.tsv", mustWork = TRUE))
extension <- normalizePath(Sys.getenv("DUCKHTS_EXTENSION", "build/release/duckhts.duckdb_extension"),
                           mustWork = TRUE)
duckdb_cli <- Sys.getenv("DUCKDB_CLI", Sys.which("duckdb"))
stopifnot(nzchar(duckdb_cli), file.exists("/usr/bin/time"))
duckdb_runtime <- system2(duckdb_cli, "--version", stdout = TRUE)[[1L]]
revision <- system2("git", c("rev-parse", "HEAD"), stdout = TRUE)
src_tree <- system2("git", c("rev-parse", "HEAD:src"), stdout = TRUE)
if (system2("git", c("diff", "--quiet", "HEAD", "--", "src"), stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE) != 0L) {
  stop("Build source must match the recorded HEAD")
}
host_load <- sub(".*load average: ", "", system2("uptime", stdout = TRUE))
quote_literal <- function(value) paste0("'", gsub("'", "''", value, fixed = TRUE), "'")
mib <- function(bytes) bytes / 2^20
whole <- function(value) format(value, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE, big.mark = ",")

source("benchmarks/bam_mismatch_stage.R")
# Stop before any staging when RBCFTools is too old to bundle samtools.
bam_mismatch_tool("samtools")
samtools_version <- RBCFTools::samtools_version()
rbcftools_version <- as.character(utils::packageVersion("RBCFTools"))

# One untimed SQL script in its own CLI process; the rows of its last
# statement come back, as numbers unless `numeric` is FALSE.
query_untimed <- function(sql, numeric = TRUE) {
  output <- suppressWarnings(system2(duckdb_cli, c("-unsigned", "-csv", "-bail"),
                                     input = c(sprintf("LOAD %s;", quote_literal(extension)), sql),
                                     stdout = TRUE))
  if (!is.null(attr(output, "status"))) stop("DuckDB CLI failed on an untimed query", call. = FALSE)
  utils::read.csv(text = output, colClasses = if (numeric) "numeric" else "character")
}

reference_argument <- function(reference) {
  if (is.null(reference) || is.na(reference)) "" else paste0(", reference := ", quote_literal(reference))
}

# Run one query in a fresh CLI process with the given threads and spill
# forbidden; its single row comes back with latency and memory.
run_fresh <- function(query, threads) {
  scratch <- tempfile("mate-overlap-scaling-")
  dir.create(scratch)
  on.exit(unlink(scratch, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  sql_path <- file.path(scratch, "query.sql")
  result_path <- file.path(scratch, "result.csv")
  profile_path <- file.path(scratch, "profile.json")
  time_path <- file.path(scratch, "time.tsv")
  writeLines(c(
    sprintf("SET threads = %d;", threads),
    "SET max_temp_directory_size = '0KiB';",
    sprintf("LOAD %s;", quote_literal(extension)),
    "PRAGMA enable_profiling = 'json';",
    sprintf("PRAGMA profiling_output = %s;", quote_literal(profile_path)),
    sprintf("COPY (%s) TO %s (HEADER);", query, quote_literal(result_path)),
    "PRAGMA disable_profiling;"
  ), sql_path)
  status <- system2("/usr/bin/time", c("-f", shQuote("%M\t%e"), "-o", shQuote(time_path),
                                       shQuote(duckdb_cli), "-unsigned", "-batch", "-bail"),
                    stdin = sql_path, stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE)
  if (status != 0L) stop("DuckDB CLI failed (status ", status, ")")
  profile <- jsonlite::fromJSON(profile_path, simplifyVector = TRUE)
  timing <- utils::read.delim(time_path, header = FALSE, col.names = c("max_rss_kib", "process_seconds"))
  data.frame(utils::read.csv(result_path, colClasses = "numeric"),
             seconds = as.numeric(profile$latency), max_rss_kib = timing$max_rss_kib[[1L]],
             peak_buffer_bytes = as.numeric(profile$system_peak_buffer_memory),
             peak_temp_bytes = as.numeric(profile$system_peak_temp_dir_size))
}

count_query <- function(path, region, reference) sprintf(paste(
  "SELECT count(*) AS output_rows, sum(positions)::BIGINT AS positions,",
  "coalesce(sum(positions) FILTER (WHERE read1_base != read2_base), 0)::BIGINT AS disagreements",
  "FROM duckhts_bam_mate_overlap_counts(%s, region := %s%s)"),
  quote_literal(path), quote_literal(region), reference_argument(reference))

# The held-mate derivation described above. `source` is a read_bam() call;
# each row of `regions` names a label, a contig and the last position of the
# region. Each region gets both bounds, the position where the lower bound is
# reached, the pairs held, the kept alignments, the kept alignments without a
# matching CIGAR and sequence, the longest kept alignment's CIGAR, sequence
# and qualities in bytes, the names with two kept alignments that do not
# pair, and the most kept alignments of one name in the input. The
# derivation holds only for names with at most two kept alignments and for
# kept alignments whose CIGAR matches their sequence; callers check.
held_replay <- function(source, regions) {
  region_values <- paste(sprintf("(%s, %s, %.0f)", quote_literal(regions$label), quote_literal(regions$contig),
                                 regions$region_end), collapse = ", ")
  # `paired`: the two kept alignments of a name pair as the function requires,
  # one read 1 and one read 2, each naming the other's start. With two rows,
  # PNEXT + POS is then the same on both and equals min(POS) + max(POS).
  sql <- c(
    "CREATE TEMP TABLE names AS",
    "SELECT RNAME, QNAME, count(*) AS kept_mates, count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT has_bases) AS without_bases,",
    "  min(POS) AS first_pos, max(POS) AS last_pos,",
    "  arg_min(PNEXT, POS) AS first_mate_pos, arg_min(span, POS) AS first_span, max(bytes) AS bytes,",
    "  count(*) = 2 AND count(*) FILTER (WHERE mate_bits = 64) = 1 AND count(*) FILTER (WHERE mate_bits = 128) = 1",
    "    AND min(PNEXT + POS) = max(PNEXT + POS) AND min(PNEXT + POS) = min(POS) + max(POS) AS paired",
    "FROM (",
    "  SELECT RNAME, QNAME, POS, PNEXT, FLAG & 192 AS mate_bits, cigar_reference_length(CIGAR) AS span,",
    "    coalesce(len(SEQ) > 0 AND cigar_query_length(CIGAR) = len(SEQ), false) AS has_bases,",
    "    4 * len(regexp_extract_all(CIGAR, '[0-9]+[MIDNSHP=X]')) + (len(SEQ) + 1) // 2 + len(SEQ) AS bytes",
    sprintf("  FROM %s", source),
    "  WHERE (FLAG & 3844) = 0 AND MAPQ >= 20 AND (FLAG & 1) != 0 AND (FLAG & 8) = 0 AND RNEXT = RNAME",
    ") kept",
    "GROUP BY RNAME, QNAME;",
    "CREATE TEMP TABLE holds AS",
    "SELECT RNAME, first_pos AS hold_pos,",
    "  CASE WHEN paired THEN last_pos ELSE first_mate_pos + 1 END AS release_pos, paired AS taken",
    "FROM names",
    "WHERE first_mate_pos >= first_pos AND first_mate_pos < first_pos + first_span;",
    "CREATE TEMP TABLE trajectory AS",
    "WITH events AS (",
    "  SELECT RNAME, hold_pos AS pos, 1 AS holds, 0 AS takes, 0 AS drops FROM holds",
    "  UNION ALL",
    "  SELECT RNAME, release_pos, 0, CASE WHEN taken THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, CASE WHEN taken THEN 0 ELSE 1 END",
    "  FROM holds",
    "), per_position AS (",
    "  SELECT RNAME, pos, sum(holds) AS holds, sum(takes) AS takes, sum(drops) AS drops",
    "  FROM events GROUP BY RNAME, pos",
    ")",
    "SELECT RNAME, pos, takes,",
    "  sum(holds - takes - drops) OVER (PARTITION BY RNAME ORDER BY pos ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS held_after",
    "FROM per_position;",
    sprintf("WITH regions(label, contig, region_end) AS (VALUES %s),", region_values),
    "held AS (",
    "  SELECT r.label, max(t.held_after) AS held_lower, max(t.held_after + t.takes) AS held_upper,",
    "    arg_max(t.pos, t.held_after) AS peak_pos",
    "  FROM regions r JOIN trajectory t ON t.RNAME = r.contig AND t.pos <= r.region_end",
    "  GROUP BY r.label",
    "), held_pairs AS (",
    "  SELECT r.label, count(*) AS pairs_held",
    "  FROM regions r JOIN holds h ON h.RNAME = r.contig AND h.hold_pos <= r.region_end",
    "  GROUP BY r.label",
    "), kept AS (",
    "  SELECT r.label,",
    "    sum(CASE WHEN n.first_pos <= r.region_end THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +",
    "        CASE WHEN n.kept_mates = 2 AND n.last_pos <= r.region_end THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS kept_alignments,",
    "    sum(n.without_bases) AS without_bases, max(n.bytes) AS longest_bytes,",
    "    count(*) FILTER (WHERE n.kept_mates = 2 AND NOT n.paired) AS unpaired_names",
    "  FROM regions r JOIN names n ON n.RNAME = r.contig AND n.first_pos <= r.region_end",
    "  GROUP BY r.label",
    ")",
    "SELECT label, held_lower, held_upper, peak_pos, pairs_held, kept_alignments, without_bases, longest_bytes,",
    "  unpaired_names, (SELECT max(kept_mates) FROM names) AS most_kept_per_name",
    "FROM held JOIN held_pairs USING (label) JOIN kept USING (label) ORDER BY label;")
  replay <- query_untimed(sql, numeric = FALSE)
  for (column in setdiff(names(replay), "label")) replay[[column]] <- as.numeric(replay[[column]])
  replay <- replay[match(regions$label, replay$label), ]
  rownames(replay) <- NULL
  replay
}

# Run the function untimed with `max_pending` set; it succeeds or returns the
# error text.
run_with_limit <- function(path, region, reference, max_pending) {
  sql <- c(sprintf("LOAD %s;", quote_literal(extension)),
           sprintf(paste("SELECT count(*) AS output_rows FROM duckhts_bam_mate_overlap_counts(%s, region := %s%s,",
                         "max_pending := %.0f);"),
                   quote_literal(path), quote_literal(region), reference_argument(reference), max_pending))
  output <- suppressWarnings(system2(duckdb_cli, c("-unsigned", "-batch", "-bail", "-csv"), input = sql,
                                     stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE))
  list(succeeded = is.null(attr(output, "status")), text = paste(output, collapse = "\n"))
}

# The function holds at most `upper` mates of this input and more than
# `lower` - 1: it succeeds at the first limit and fails at the second.
held_limit_agrees <- function(path, region, reference, lower, upper) {
  at_upper <- run_with_limit(path, region, reference, upper)
  below_lower <- run_with_limit(path, region, reference, lower - 1)
  limit_error <- sprintf("more than max_pending (%.0f) mates wait for their mate", lower - 1)
  at_upper$succeeded && !below_lower$succeeded && grepl(limit_error, below_lower$text, fixed = TRUE)
}

# The live state of the budget, in bytes.
counter_bytes <- 95 * 95 * 16 * 8
held_state_bytes <- function(held, longest_bytes) {
  entries <- 1024 * ceiling(held / 1024)
  table_entries <- 1024 * 2^pmax(0, ceiling(log2(pmax(held, 1) / 1024)))
  table_bytes <- ifelse(table_entries > 1024, 24 * (3 * table_entries + 2), 24 * (2 * 1024 + 1))
  entries * (320 + 16) + table_bytes + held * (longest_bytes + 24)
}

# ---- the real input ----
slice_id <- "bam_mismatch_hg00403_chr1_cram"
slice_identity <- bam_mismatch_check_staged(slice_id, extension)
cram <- duckhtsbench::duckhts_bench_artifact_path(slice_id)
reference <- duckhtsbench::duckhts_bench_artifact_path("liftover_grch38_fasta")
duckhtsbench::duckhts_bench_validate_identity("liftover_grch38_fasta", reference)
# The slice is one whole contig; its length comes from the reference index.
contig <- bam_mismatch_registry_row(slice_id)$fields[["region"]]
reference_index <- utils::read.delim(paste0(reference, ".fai"), header = FALSE)
contig_length <- reference_index[[2L]][reference_index[[1L]] == contig]
stopifnot(length(contig_length) == 1L)
# The real series reads the whole contig; a reduced render reads a 2 Mb
# window around the most held mates instead.
window <- if (reduced) c(124000001, 126000000) else c(1, contig_length)
window_region <- sprintf("%s:%.0f-%.0f", contig, window[[1L]], window[[2L]])
# The CRAM index lists each slice's start and reference span, in file order.
slices <- utils::read.delim(gzfile(paste0(cram, ".crai")), header = FALSE,
                            col.names = c("sequence", "start", "span", "container", "slice", "size"))
consecutive_span <- slices$span + c(0, utils::head(slices$span, -1L))
# The slices that a region from the window start to `region_end` reads.
slices_read <- function(region_end) slices$start <= region_end & slices$start + slices$span > window[[1L]]

# Untimed staging: the region ends at which a quarter and a half of the
# alignments of the window have started, and the alignments of each region.
cuts <- query_untimed(c(
  sprintf("CREATE TEMP TABLE starts AS SELECT POS FROM read_bam(%s, reference := %s, region := %s);",
          quote_literal(cram), quote_literal(reference), quote_literal(window_region)),
  "CREATE TEMP TABLE cuts AS",
  "SELECT quantile_disc(POS, 0.25)::BIGINT AS quarter, quantile_disc(POS, 0.5)::BIGINT AS half FROM starts;",
  "SELECT quarter, half, (SELECT count(*) FROM starts WHERE POS <= quarter) AS alignments_1x,",
  "  (SELECT count(*) FROM starts WHERE POS <= half) AS alignments_2x,",
  "  (SELECT count(*) FROM starts) AS alignments_4x FROM cuts;"))
stopifnot(nrow(cuts) == 1L, cuts$quarter < cuts$half, cuts$half < window[[2L]])
# The whole contig holds every alignment of the slice.
if (!reduced) stopifnot(cuts$alignments_4x == slice_identity$alignments)
real <- data.frame(cell = c("1", "2", "4"), scale = c(1L, 2L, 4L),
                   region_end = c(cuts$quarter, cuts$half, window[[2L]]),
                   alignments = c(cuts$alignments_1x, cuts$alignments_2x, cuts$alignments_4x))
real$region <- sprintf("%s:%.0f-%.0f", contig, window[[1L]], real$region_end)
real$reference_span <- vapply(real$region_end, function(end) max(consecutive_span[slices_read(end)]), 0)

real_held <- held_replay(sprintf("read_bam(%s, reference := %s, region := %s)", quote_literal(cram),
                                 quote_literal(reference), quote_literal(window_region)),
                         data.frame(label = real$cell, contig = contig, region_end = real$region_end))
stopifnot(all(real_held$without_bases == 0), all(real_held$most_kept_per_name <= 2),
          all(real_held$held_lower >= 2), all(real_held$held_lower <= real_held$held_upper))
real <- cbind(real, real_held[setdiff(names(real_held), "label")])
real$limit_agrees <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(real)), function(k) {
  held_limit_agrees(cram, real$region[[k]], reference, real$held_lower[[k]], real$held_upper[[k]])
}, logical(1L))
stopifnot(all(real$limit_agrees))
real$htslib_bytes <- 32 * 2^20 + real$reference_span

# The counts of the function in the 400 kb around the position where the most
# mates are held, against the same count made in SQL. A pair shares a
# position only if each mate starts before the other ends, so the SQL count
# keeps the alignments that can: the mate starts before this one ends, and
# this one starts within the longest kept span after the mate.
peak_pos <- real$peak_pos[real$scale == 4L]
oracle_start <- max(window[[1L]], peak_pos - 2e5)
oracle_end <- min(window[[2L]], peak_pos + 2e5)
oracle_region <- sprintf("%s:%.0f-%.0f", contig, oracle_start, oracle_end)
oracle <- query_untimed(c(
  "CREATE TEMP TABLE observed AS",
  sprintf("SELECT * FROM duckhts_bam_mate_overlap_counts(%s, reference := %s, region := %s);",
          quote_literal(cram), quote_literal(reference), quote_literal(oracle_region)),
  "CREATE TEMP TABLE expected AS",
  "WITH filtered AS (",
  "  SELECT QNAME, FLAG, RNAME, POS, PNEXT, SEQ, QUAL, CIGAR, cigar_reference_length(CIGAR) AS span",
  sprintf("  FROM read_bam(%s, reference := %s, region := %s)",
          quote_literal(cram), quote_literal(reference), quote_literal(oracle_region)),
  "  WHERE (FLAG & 3844) = 0 AND MAPQ >= 20 AND (FLAG & 1) != 0 AND (FLAG & 8) = 0 AND RNEXT = RNAME",
  "), reads AS (",
  "  SELECT QNAME, FLAG, RNAME, POS, PNEXT, SEQ, QUAL, cigar_aligned_blocks(CIGAR, POS) AS blocks",
  "  FROM filtered",
  "  WHERE PNEXT < POS + span AND POS < PNEXT + (SELECT max(span) FROM filtered)",
  "), aligned AS (",
  "  SELECT QNAME, FLAG, RNAME, POS, PNEXT, SEQ, QUAL, unnest(blocks.ref_start) AS ref_start,",
  "    unnest(blocks.query_start) AS query_start, unnest(blocks.width) AS width",
  "  FROM reads",
  "), read_bases AS (",
  "  SELECT QNAME, FLAG, RNAME, POS, PNEXT, ref_start + i AS ref_pos, substr(SEQ, query_start + i + 1, 1) AS base,",
  "    CASE WHEN QUAL IS NULL OR QUAL = '*' THEN NULL",
  "         ELSE least(ord(substr(QUAL, query_start + i + 1, 1)) - 33, 93) END AS quality",
  "  FROM aligned, LATERAL (SELECT unnest(range(width)) AS i)",
  ")",
  "SELECT r1.quality AS read1_quality, r2.quality AS read2_quality, r1.base AS read1_base, r2.base AS read2_base,",
  "  count(*) AS positions",
  "FROM read_bases r1 JOIN read_bases r2",
  "  ON r1.QNAME = r2.QNAME AND r1.RNAME = r2.RNAME AND r1.ref_pos = r2.ref_pos",
  "WHERE (r1.FLAG & 192) = 64 AND (r2.FLAG & 192) = 128 AND r1.PNEXT = r2.POS AND r2.PNEXT = r1.POS",
  "  AND r1.base IN ('A', 'C', 'G', 'T') AND r2.base IN ('A', 'C', 'G', 'T')",
  "GROUP BY ALL;",
  "SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM observed) AS observed_rows, (SELECT count(*) FROM expected) AS expected_rows,",
  "  (SELECT sum(positions) FROM expected) AS expected_positions,",
  "  (SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT * FROM observed EXCEPT ALL SELECT * FROM expected)) AS extra_rows,",
  "  (SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT * FROM expected EXCEPT ALL SELECT * FROM observed)) AS missing_rows,",
  "  region_alignments, region_bases,",
  sprintf("  %.0f AS region_length", oracle_end - oracle_start + 1),
  "FROM (SELECT count(*) AS region_alignments, sum(len(SEQ)) AS region_bases",
  sprintf("      FROM read_bam(%s, reference := %s, region := %s));",
          quote_literal(cram), quote_literal(reference), quote_literal(oracle_region))))
stopifnot(oracle$expected_rows > 0, oracle$observed_rows == oracle$expected_rows,
          oracle$extra_rows == 0, oracle$missing_rows == 0)

# ---- the synthetic input ----
read_length <- 150L
amplicon_length <- 2L * read_length
family_spacing <- 1000L
first_start <- 1001L
# A fixed amplicon from the Park-Miller generator; every product is exact in a double.
amplicon <- local({
  state <- 20261012
  bases <- character(amplicon_length)
  for (i in seq_len(amplicon_length)) {
    state <- (16807 * state) %% 2147483647
    bases[[i]] <- c("A", "C", "G", "T")[state %/% 536870912 + 1]
  }
  paste(bases, collapse = "")
})
amplicon_bases <- strsplit(amplicon, "", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
read1_quality <- ifelse(seq_len(read_length) %% 4L == 0L, 23L, 37L)
read2_quality <- ifelse(seq_len(read_length) %% 3L == 0L, 12L, 37L)
quality_text <- function(quality) intToUtf8(quality + 33L)
# A reduced render keeps the families and holds a hundredth of the pairs.
pair_scale <- if (reduced) 0.01 else 1
synthetic <- data.frame(cell = c("c11", "c21", "c41", "c12", "c14", "c22", "c44"),
                        families = c(4L, 8L, 16L, 2L, 1L, 4L, 4L),
                        pairs = c(1e5, 1e5, 1e5, 2e5, 4e5, 2e5, 4e5) * pair_scale, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
synthetic$alignments <- 2 * synthetic$families * synthetic$pairs
synthetic$length <- first_start + family_spacing * synthetic$families + family_spacing
series <- data.frame(series = rep(c("alignments", "held mates", "both"), each = 3L),
                     scale = rep(c(1L, 2L, 4L), times = 3L),
                     cell = c("c11", "c21", "c41", "c11", "c12", "c14", "c11", "c22", "c44"),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

synthetic_dir <- tempfile("mate-overlap-synthetic-")
dir.create(synthetic_dir)
sam <- file.path(synthetic_dir, "synthetic.sam")
body <- file.path(synthetic_dir, "body.sam")
bam <- file.path(synthetic_dir, "synthetic.bam")
writeLines(c("@HD\tVN:1.6\tSO:unsorted", sprintf("@SQ\tSN:%s\tLN:%d", synthetic$cell, synthetic$length)), sam)
contig_values <- paste(sprintf("(%s, %d, %.0f)", quote_literal(synthetic$cell), synthetic$families,
                               synthetic$pairs), collapse = ", ")
generate <- c(
  sprintf("COPY (WITH contigs(contig, families, pairs) AS (VALUES %s),", contig_values),
  "fragments AS (",
  sprintf("  SELECT contig, f, j, %d + %d * f AS start, 1 + (97 * j) %% 149 AS d", first_start, family_spacing),
  "  FROM contigs, LATERAL range(families) family(f), LATERAL range(pairs) pair(j)",
  "), mates AS (",
  sprintf("  SELECT *, substr(%s, d + 1, %d) AS read2, (j // 16) %% (%d - d) AS o FROM fragments",
          quote_literal(amplicon), read_length, read_length),
  ")",
  "SELECT concat_ws(chr(9), contig || ':' || f || ':' || j, '99', contig, start, '60', '150M', '=', start + d,",
  sprintf("  d + 150, %s, %s)", quote_literal(substr(amplicon, 1L, read_length)),
          quote_literal(quality_text(read1_quality))),
  "FROM mates",
  "UNION ALL",
  "SELECT concat_ws(chr(9), contig || ':' || f || ':' || j, '147', contig, start + d,",
  "  CASE WHEN j % 16 = 15 THEN '10' ELSE '60' END, '150M', '=', start, -(d + 150),",
  "  CASE WHEN j % 16 = 7",
  "       THEN substr(read2, 1, o) || translate(substr(read2, o + 1, 1), 'ACGT', 'CGTA') || substr(read2, o + 2)",
  "       ELSE read2 END,",
  sprintf("  %s)", quote_literal(quality_text(read2_quality))),
  sprintf("FROM mates) TO %s (FORMAT CSV, HEADER FALSE, QUOTE '', ESCAPE '');", quote_literal(body)))
status <- system2(duckdb_cli, c("-batch", "-bail"), input = generate)
if (status != 0L) stop("could not write the synthetic SAM", call. = FALSE)
stopifnot(file.append(sam, body))
unlink(body)
bam_mismatch_run("samtools", c("sort", "--no-PG", "-@", "3", "-m", "512M", "-T", file.path(synthetic_dir, "sort"),
                               "-o", bam, sam))
bam_mismatch_run("samtools", c("index", bam))
unlink(sam)

# The BAM has the alignments and positions of the design.
synthetic_identity <- query_untimed(sprintf(
  "SELECT RNAME AS cell, count(*) AS alignments, sum(POS) AS position_sum FROM read_bam(%s) GROUP BY RNAME;",
  quote_literal(bam)), numeric = FALSE)
synthetic_identity <- synthetic_identity[match(synthetic$cell, synthetic_identity$cell), ]
offset_sum <- function(pairs) sum(1 + (97 * (seq_len(pairs) - 1)) %% 149)
design_position_sum <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(synthetic)), function(k) {
  families <- synthetic$families[[k]]
  family_starts <- first_start + family_spacing * (seq_len(families) - 1)
  2 * synthetic$pairs[[k]] * sum(family_starts) + families * offset_sum(synthetic$pairs[[k]])
}, numeric(1L))
stopifnot(identical(as.numeric(synthetic_identity$alignments), synthetic$alignments),
          identical(as.numeric(synthetic_identity$position_sum), design_position_sum))

# The counts that follow from the design: each counted pair shares amplicon
# offsets d to 149 (zero-based) with its read 1; a pair with j mod 16 = 15 is
# not counted; a pair with j mod 16 = 7 has read 2's base at shared offset
# (j div 16) mod (150 - d) moved one step along A, C, G, T.
substitute_base <- c(A = "C", C = "G", G = "T", T = "A")
design_counts <- function(families, pairs) {
  j <- seq_len(pairs) - 1
  d <- 1 + (97 * j) %% 149
  counted <- j %% 16 != 15
  shared <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(149L), function(offset) data.frame(d = offset, a = offset:149)))
  shared$pairs <- tabulate(d[counted], nbins = 149L)[shared$d]
  agreeing <- data.frame(read1_quality = read1_quality[shared$a + 1], read2_quality = read2_quality[shared$a - shared$d + 1],
                         read1_base = amplicon_bases[shared$a + 1], read2_base = amplicon_bases[shared$a + 1],
                         positions = shared$pairs)
  changed <- j %% 16 == 7
  o <- (j[changed] %/% 16) %% (150 - d[changed])
  a <- d[changed] + o
  moved <- data.frame(read1_quality = read1_quality[a + 1], read2_quality = read2_quality[o + 1],
                      read1_base = amplicon_bases[a + 1], read2_base = amplicon_bases[a + 1], positions = -1)
  substituted <- moved
  substituted$read2_base <- unname(substitute_base[moved$read1_base])
  substituted$positions <- 1
  counts <- stats::aggregate(positions ~ read1_quality + read2_quality + read1_base + read2_base,
                             data = rbind(agreeing, moved, substituted), FUN = sum)
  counts <- counts[counts$positions > 0, ]
  counts$positions <- counts$positions * families
  counts
}
row_keys <- function(rows) {
  sort(paste(rows$read1_quality, rows$read2_quality, rows$read1_base, rows$read2_base,
             format(as.numeric(rows$positions), scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)))
}
synthetic_checks <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(synthetic)), function(k) {
  expected <- design_counts(synthetic$families[[k]], synthetic$pairs[[k]])
  observed <- query_untimed(sprintf("SELECT * FROM duckhts_bam_mate_overlap_counts(%s, region := %s);",
                                    quote_literal(bam), quote_literal(synthetic$cell[[k]])), numeric = FALSE)
  data.frame(cell = synthetic$cell[[k]], expected_rows = nrow(expected), observed_rows = nrow(observed),
             expected_positions = sum(expected$positions),
             expected_disagreements = sum(expected$positions[expected$read1_base != expected$read2_base]),
             rows_equal = identical(row_keys(observed), row_keys(expected)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
stopifnot(all(synthetic_checks$rows_equal))

synthetic_held <- held_replay(sprintf("read_bam(%s)", quote_literal(bam)),
                              data.frame(label = synthetic$cell, contig = synthetic$cell,
                                         region_end = synthetic$length))
stopifnot(all(synthetic_held$without_bases == 0), all(synthetic_held$most_kept_per_name <= 2),
          all(synthetic_held$held_lower == synthetic$pairs), all(synthetic_held$held_upper == synthetic$pairs))
synthetic <- cbind(synthetic, synthetic_held[setdiff(names(synthetic_held), "label")])
synthetic$limit_agrees <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(synthetic)), function(k) {
  held_limit_agrees(bam, synthetic$cell[[k]], NULL, synthetic$held_lower[[k]], synthetic$held_upper[[k]])
}, logical(1L))
stopifnot(all(synthetic$limit_agrees))
synthetic$htslib_bytes <- 4 * 2^20

# ---- the budget, before any measurement ----
empty_runs <- vapply(seq_len(3L), function(run) run_fresh("SELECT 1 AS output_rows", 1L)$max_rss_kib, numeric(1L))
overhead_mib <- median(empty_runs) / 1024
memory_limit <- system2(duckdb_cli, c("-list", "-noheader"),
                        input = "SELECT current_setting('memory_limit');", stdout = TRUE)[[1L]]
budget <- function(cells) {
  cells$held_mib <- mib(held_state_bytes(cells$held_upper, cells$longest_bytes))
  cells$live_mib <- mib(counter_bytes) + cells$held_mib + mib(cells$htslib_bytes)
  cells$model_mib <- overhead_mib + cells$live_mib
  cells$ceiling_mib <- overhead_mib + 3 * cells$live_mib
  cells
}
real <- budget(real)
synthetic <- budget(synthetic)

# ---- the measurements ----
cells <- rbind(
  data.frame(workload = "real", cell = real$cell, path = cram, region = real$region, reference = reference,
             model_mib = real$model_mib, ceiling_mib = real$ceiling_mib, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  data.frame(workload = "synthetic", cell = synthetic$cell, path = bam, region = synthetic$cell, reference = NA,
             model_mib = synthetic$model_mib, ceiling_mib = synthetic$ceiling_mib, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
observations <- list()
for (repetition in 1:3) {
  order <- if (repetition %% 2L == 1L) seq_len(nrow(cells)) else rev(seq_len(nrow(cells)))
  for (threads in c(1L, 4L)) {
    for (k in order) {
      observed <- run_fresh(count_query(cells$path[[k]], cells$region[[k]], cells$reference[[k]]), threads)
      observations[[length(observations) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
        workload = cells$workload[[k]], cell = cells$cell[[k]], region = cells$region[[k]], threads = threads,
        repetition = repetition, observed, model_mib = cells$model_mib[[k]], ceiling_mib = cells$ceiling_mib[[k]],
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }
  }
}
runs <- do.call(rbind, observations)
unlink(synthetic_dir, recursive = TRUE)
stopifnot(all(runs$peak_temp_bytes == 0), all(runs$positions > 0))
runs_path <- if (reduced) {
  tempfile("mate-overlap-runs-", fileext = ".csv")
} else {
  "benchmarks/benchmark_bam_mate_overlap_counts_runs.csv"
}
write.csv(runs, runs_path, row.names = FALSE)
over_budget <- runs[runs$max_rss_kib / 1024 > runs$ceiling_mib, ]
if (nrow(over_budget)) {
  print(over_budget[c("workload", "cell", "threads", "max_rss_kib", "ceiling_mib")])
  stop("observations exceed the declared memory budget", call. = FALSE)
}
# Reported, not gated: observations whose peak RSS is above overhead + live state.
above_model <- runs[runs$max_rss_kib / 1024 > runs$model_mib, ]

summarise_cells <- function(rows) {
  groups <- split(rows, list(rows$cell, rows$threads), drop = TRUE)
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(groups, function(group) {
    # Every repetition of a cell must give the same counts.
    stopifnot(length(unique(group$output_rows)) == 1L, length(unique(group$positions)) == 1L,
              length(unique(group$disagreements)) == 1L)
    data.frame(cell = group$cell[[1L]], threads = group$threads[[1L]], output_rows = group$output_rows[[1L]],
               positions = group$positions[[1L]], disagreements = group$disagreements[[1L]],
               median_seconds = median(group$seconds), min_seconds = min(group$seconds),
               max_seconds = max(group$seconds), median_rss_mib = round(median(group$max_rss_kib) / 1024, 1),
               max_rss_mib = round(max(group$max_rss_kib) / 1024, 1),
               max_buffer_mib = round(max(group$peak_buffer_bytes) / 2^20, 1), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}
# The counts of a cell must be the same at both thread settings.
same_at_both_thread_settings <- function(summary) {
  counted <- c("cell", "output_rows", "positions", "disagreements")
  one <- summary[summary$threads == 1L, counted]
  four <- summary[summary$threads == 4L, counted]
  isTRUE(all.equal(one[order(one$cell), ], four[order(four$cell), ], check.attributes = FALSE))
}

real_summary <- summarise_cells(runs[runs$workload == "real", ])
stopifnot(same_at_both_thread_settings(real_summary))
real_summary <- merge(real[c("cell", "scale", "alignments", "held_upper", "model_mib", "ceiling_mib")], real_summary,
                      by = "cell")
real_summary <- real_summary[order(real_summary$threads, real_summary$scale), ]
real_summary$model_mib <- round(real_summary$model_mib, 1)
real_summary$ceiling_mib <- round(real_summary$ceiling_mib, 1)
rownames(real_summary) <- NULL
real_exponents <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(real_summary, real_summary$threads), function(s) {
  s <- s[order(s$scale), ]
  growth <- function(low, high) {
    log(s$median_seconds[[high]] / s$median_seconds[[low]]) / log(s$alignments[[high]] / s$alignments[[low]])
  }
  data.frame(threads = s$threads[[1L]], one_x_seconds = s$median_seconds[[1L]],
             alignments_ratio_2x = s$alignments[[2L]] / s$alignments[[1L]],
             alignments_ratio_4x = s$alignments[[3L]] / s$alignments[[2L]],
             time_exponent_2x = growth(1L, 2L), time_exponent_4x = growth(2L, 3L),
             rss_ratio_2x = s$median_rss_mib[[2L]] / s$median_rss_mib[[1L]],
             rss_ratio_4x = s$median_rss_mib[[3L]] / s$median_rss_mib[[1L]])
}))
rownames(real_exponents) <- NULL
real_one <- real_summary[real_summary$threads == 1L, ]
# The timing verdict; a reduced render is too short to give one.
if (!reduced) {
  stopifnot(real_one$median_seconds[real_one$scale == 1L] >= 5,
            all(real_exponents$time_exponent_2x <= 1.25), all(real_exponents$time_exponent_4x <= 1.25))
}

synthetic_summary <- summarise_cells(runs[runs$workload == "synthetic", ])
stopifnot(same_at_both_thread_settings(synthetic_summary))
checked <- merge(synthetic_summary, synthetic_checks, by = "cell")
stopifnot(all(checked$output_rows == checked$expected_rows), all(checked$positions == checked$expected_positions),
          all(checked$disagreements == checked$expected_disagreements))
synthetic_series <- merge(series, synthetic[c("cell", "families", "pairs", "alignments", "held_upper", "model_mib",
                                              "ceiling_mib")], by = "cell")
synthetic_series <- merge(synthetic_series, synthetic_summary, by = "cell")
synthetic_series$series <- factor(synthetic_series$series, levels = c("alignments", "held mates", "both"))
synthetic_series <- synthetic_series[order(synthetic_series$series, synthetic_series$threads, synthetic_series$scale), ]
synthetic_series$series <- as.character(synthetic_series$series)
synthetic_series$model_mib <- round(synthetic_series$model_mib, 1)
synthetic_series$ceiling_mib <- round(synthetic_series$ceiling_mib, 1)
rownames(synthetic_series) <- NULL
synthetic_growth <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(synthetic_series, list(synthetic_series$series, synthetic_series$threads),
                                                drop = TRUE), function(s) {
  s <- s[order(s$scale), ]
  data.frame(series = s$series[[1L]], threads = s$threads[[1L]], one_x_seconds = s$median_seconds[[1L]],
             time_ratio_2x = s$median_seconds[[2L]] / s$median_seconds[[1L]],
             time_ratio_4x = s$median_seconds[[3L]] / s$median_seconds[[2L]],
             rss_mib_1x = s$median_rss_mib[[1L]], rss_mib_2x = s$median_rss_mib[[2L]],
             rss_mib_4x = s$median_rss_mib[[3L]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
synthetic_growth$series <- factor(synthetic_growth$series, levels = c("alignments", "held mates", "both"))
synthetic_growth <- synthetic_growth[order(synthetic_growth$series, synthetic_growth$threads), ]
synthetic_growth$series <- as.character(synthetic_growth$series)
rownames(synthetic_growth) <- NULL

# What one more held mate costs: the peak RSS of the held-mates series on one
# thread against its held-mate count, beside the same slope of the model.
held_ends <- series$cell[series$series == "held mates" & series$scale %in% c(1L, 4L)]
held_rss <- synthetic_summary[synthetic_summary$threads == 1L, ]
held_rss_mib <- held_rss$median_rss_mib[match(held_ends, held_rss$cell)]
held_model <- synthetic[match(held_ends, synthetic$cell), ]
held_added <- held_model$held_upper[[2L]] - held_model$held_upper[[1L]]
measured_bytes_per_mate <- (held_rss_mib[[2L]] - held_rss_mib[[1L]]) * 2^20 / held_added
model_bytes_per_mate <- (held_model$model_mib[[2L]] - held_model$model_mib[[1L]]) * 2^20 / held_added
# The real series: what the model charges at 4x for the held mates and for
# the reference of the widest pair of consecutive slices; the widest slice
# that the 4x region reads, and whether the 2x region reads it too.
real_largest <- real[real$scale == 4L, ]
slices_4x <- slices[slices_read(real_largest$region_end), ]
widest_slice <- slices_4x[which.max(slices_4x$span), ]
widest_read_at_2x <- widest_slice$start <= real$region_end[real$scale == 2L]
peak_past_2x <- peak_pos > real$region_end[real$scale == 2L]

# Untimed: the 4x region by the lower of the two base qualities.
by_quality <- query_untimed(sprintf(paste(
  "SELECT least(read1_quality, read2_quality) AS lower_quality, sum(positions)::BIGINT AS positions,",
  "coalesce(sum(positions) FILTER (WHERE read1_base != read2_base), 0)::BIGINT AS disagreements",
  "FROM duckhts_bam_mate_overlap_counts(%s, reference := %s, region := %s)",
  "GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY lower_quality NULLS LAST;"),
  quote_literal(cram), quote_literal(reference), quote_literal(real$region[real$scale == 4L])))
largest <- real_one[real_one$scale == 4L, ]
stopifnot(sum(by_quality$positions) == largest$positions, sum(by_quality$disagreements) == largest$disagreements)
by_quality$disagreement_rate <- by_quality$disagreements / by_quality$positions
by_quality$share_of_positions <- by_quality$positions / sum(by_quality$positions)
```

Source revision: `r revision`; `src` tree `r src_tree`. DuckDB runtime: `r duckdb_runtime` (CLI). Extension SHA-256: `r strsplit(system2("sha256sum", extension, stdout = TRUE), " ", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]][[1L]]`. samtools `r samtools_version` from RBCFTools `r rbcftools_version`. Host load at start: `r host_load`. DuckDB memory limit: `r memory_limit` (the default); temporary directory limit: 0.

Staged input: the slice has `r whole(slice_identity$alignments)` alignments (position sum `r format(slice_identity$position_sum, scientific = FALSE)`, `r whole(slice_identity$base_sum)` stored bases) in `r whole(nrow(slices))` CRAM slices. Its widest slice starts at `r whole(slices$start[which.max(slices$span)])` and spans `r whole(max(slices$span))` reference bases.

Overhead: `r round(overhead_mib, 1)` MiB.

## Inputs and budgets

Real regions. `alignments` are what the region selects, before the function's
filters; `kept_alignments` pass them. `pairs_held` are the pairs whose first
mate is held, and `unpaired_names` the names with two kept alignments that do
not pair. `held_lower` and `held_upper` bound the mates held at once, and
`limit_agrees` is TRUE when the function succeeds with `max_pending` at the
upper bound and fails one below the lower bound. `peak_pos` is where the most
mates are held. `longest_bytes` is D, `reference_span` the bases of the widest
pair of consecutive slices, and the last columns the budget in MiB: the held
mates' share, the live state, overhead + live state (`model_mib`) and the
ceiling.

```{r real-inputs, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(real[c("scale", "region", "alignments", "kept_alignments", "pairs_held", "unpaired_names",
                    "held_lower", "held_upper", "limit_agrees", "peak_pos", "longest_bytes", "reference_span",
                    "held_mib", "live_mib", "model_mib", "ceiling_mib")],
             digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Synthetic contigs, with the same columns. The derivation finds P mates held at
once on every contig, as the design says.

```{r synthetic-inputs, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(synthetic[c("cell", "families", "pairs", "alignments", "kept_alignments", "pairs_held",
                         "unpaired_names", "held_lower", "held_upper", "limit_agrees", "longest_bytes", "held_mib",
                         "live_mib", "model_mib", "ceiling_mib")],
             digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Count checks

Each synthetic contig against the counts that follow from its design; the
measured runs reproduce the same totals:

```{r synthetic-checks, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(synthetic_checks, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

The real data in `r oracle_region`, the `r whole(oracle$region_length)` bases
around the position with the most held mates: the function gives
`r whole(oracle$observed_rows)` rows and
the SQL count `r whole(oracle$expected_rows)` rows of
`r whole(oracle$expected_positions)` shared positions, with
`r oracle$extra_rows` rows only in the function's output and
`r oracle$missing_rows` only in the SQL count.

## Measurements

The real series. `positions`, `disagreements` and `output_rows` are the result
of the query. Times are the query latency of three repetitions.

```{r real-summary, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(real_summary[c("scale", "threads", "alignments", "held_upper", "output_rows", "positions",
                            "disagreements", "median_seconds", "min_seconds", "max_seconds", "median_rss_mib",
                            "max_rss_mib", "max_buffer_mib", "model_mib", "ceiling_mib")],
             digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Growth of the median time against the alignments (an exponent of 1 is
linear), and peak-RSS ratios to 1×:

```{r real-exponents, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(real_exponents, digits = 3)
```

The synthetic series:

```{r synthetic-summary, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(synthetic_series[c("series", "scale", "cell", "threads", "alignments", "held_upper", "output_rows",
                                "positions", "disagreements", "median_seconds", "min_seconds", "max_seconds",
                                "median_rss_mib", "max_rss_mib", "max_buffer_mib", "model_mib", "ceiling_mib")],
             digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Their time ratios between doublings, reported without a verdict, and their
median peak RSS:

```{r synthetic-growth, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(synthetic_growth, digits = 3)
```

## Findings

Every observation is within its ceiling and none spills.
`r if (reduced) "A reduced render does not check the timing; the full render also stops if the 1× run of the real series on one thread takes less than 5 s or one of its time exponents is above 1.25." else "The 1× run of the real series on one thread takes at least 5 s, and none of its time exponents is above 1.25."`
The render enforces all of this. It also stops unless a cell gives the same
rows, positions and disagreements in every repetition and at both thread
settings, unless the synthetic counts equal the design's, and unless the real
counts around the most held mates equal the SQL count.

Real data: the 4× region, `r real_largest$region`, takes
`r round(largest$median_seconds, 1)` s on one thread for
`r whole(largest$alignments)` alignments, which is
`r round(largest$alignments / largest$median_seconds / 1e6, 2)` million
alignments a second, and compares `r whole(largest$positions)` shared
positions at `r largest$median_rss_mib` MiB peak RSS. The 1× region takes
`r round(real_one$median_seconds[[1L]], 1)` s at
`r real_one$median_rss_mib[[1L]]` MiB. The time exponents at one thread are
`r round(real_exponents$time_exponent_2x[real_exponents$threads == 1L], 2)` and
`r round(real_exponents$time_exponent_4x[real_exponents$threads == 1L], 2)`.

The held-mate count is not fixed in this series: it is at most
`r whole(real$held_upper[[1L]])`, `r whole(real$held_upper[[2L]])` and
`r whole(real$held_upper[[3L]])` in the three regions. The most are held at
`r whole(peak_pos)`, `r if (peak_past_2x) "past" else "before"` the end of
the 2× region, where the `r whole(oracle$region_length)` bases of the count
check hold `r whole(oracle$region_alignments)` alignments, a depth of about
`r round(oracle$region_bases / oracle$region_length)`×. At 4× the model charges
`r round(real_largest$held_mib, 1)` MiB for the held mates, and
`r round(mib(real_largest$reference_span), 1)` MiB for the reference of the
widest pair of consecutive slices. The widest slice spans
`r whole(widest_slice$span)` reference bases from
`r whole(widest_slice$start)`; `r if (widest_read_at_2x) "the 2× region reads it too" else "of the three regions, only the 4× region reads it"`.
On one thread, the median peak RSS rises by
`r round(real_one$median_rss_mib[[3L]] - real_one$median_rss_mib[[2L]], 1)` MiB
from 2× to 4×.

Synthetic data: at a fixed held-mate count of
`r whole(synthetic$pairs[[1L]])`, four times the alignments take the median
peak RSS on one thread from
`r synthetic_growth$rss_mib_1x[synthetic_growth$series == "alignments" & synthetic_growth$threads == 1L]` to
`r synthetic_growth$rss_mib_4x[synthetic_growth$series == "alignments" & synthetic_growth$threads == 1L]` MiB.
At fixed alignments, four times the held mates take it from
`r synthetic_growth$rss_mib_1x[synthetic_growth$series == "held mates" & synthetic_growth$threads == 1L]` to
`r synthetic_growth$rss_mib_4x[synthetic_growth$series == "held mates" & synthetic_growth$threads == 1L]` MiB.
Each further held mate costs `r round(measured_bytes_per_mate)` bytes of peak
RSS, and the model charges `r round(model_bytes_per_mate)` bytes.
`r if (nrow(above_model) == 0L) "No observation, real or synthetic, has a peak RSS above overhead + live state." else sprintf("%d of %d observations have a peak RSS above overhead + live state; all are within their ceiling.", nrow(above_model), nrow(runs))`
The synthetic runs take `r round(min(synthetic_summary$median_seconds), 2)` to
`r round(max(synthetic_summary$median_seconds), 2)` s, so their times carry no
verdict.

The operating scale this report supports is what it measures: one contig of
one 30× short-read sample from CRAM, and up to
`r whole(max(synthetic$pairs))` mates held at once from BAM, under the default
`max_pending` of 1,000,000. It does not measure a whole genome in one call,
long reads, or more held mates than that. The synthetic times are too short to
show whether the time per alignment grows with the held mates.

## What the counts say

The 4× region by the lower of the two base qualities of a shared position,
from one untimed run:

```{r quality, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(by_quality, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 6, 4), format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

A real allele sits on the molecule and both mates show it; a sequencing error
usually shows in one mate. So the disagreement rate is about twice the
instrument error rate. Errors made before sequencing, in the library, by PCR
or by DNA damage, show in both mates and are not seen. Only fragments shorter
than the two reads overlap, so the count leans toward short fragments and read
ends.
